Jonathan Lee Promotional Portrait

Jonathan Lee, known in Chinese as 李宗盛, is shown in a close-up portrait wearing black-framed glasses, a white collared shirt, and a dark cardigan. His gentle smile and salt-and-pepper beard are highlighted by soft, even lighting against a neutral gray background.

This image is featured on Last.fm’s artist page for 李宗盛, which lists 13.1K listeners and 425.4K scrobbles. The page also presents a detailed daily listening trend from March to September 2025 and explains the concept of scrobbling. No upcoming events are currently scheduled for the artist.

Li Zongsheng sits against a neutral backdrop, wearing a dark floral shirt and round glasses, cradling an acoustic guitar. His fingers rest lightly on the guitar body, and a smartwatch adorns his wrist. A watermark reading “头条 @梦想哥920” appears at the bottom right.

This image accompanies a Sohu article detailing Li Zongsheng’s relationship with Sandy Lam, from her early albums and his songwriting contributions to their six-year marriage and eventual separation. The article highlights his career as a music producer and her evolution into a pop icon, and recounts the story behind the classic song “为你我受冷风吹.”

Jonathan Lee Portrait

Jonathan Lee, the renowned Taiwanese singer-songwriter and producer, appears in a relaxed studio portrait. The neutral gray background and soft lighting emphasize his contemplative expression and casual attire—a white shirt under a navy blazer.

sources.title: Jonathan Lee Portfolio: 1984-1989 - album by Jonathan Lee
sources.description:
Jonathan Lee Portfolio: 1984–1989

A portrait of Jonathan Lee fills the album cover, showing the Taiwanese singer-songwriter in a yellow knit sweater and round glasses. He leans his head on his hand, gazing thoughtfully against a plain backdrop. Handwritten blue text at the center reads “1984-1989,” while bold black Chinese characters below spell out “李宗盛作品集,” indicating a collection of his works.

Released on March 21, 1989, this Mandopop compilation album gathers Jonathan Lee’s most notable songs from 1984 through 1989. The minimalist design and Lee’s relaxed pose reflect the personal and retrospective nature of the collection.
